source.title: Model 100A - Gray Whale
source.author: Digital Life / Johnson Martin; collaboration with Laurens Howle and Frank Fish; BOEM support
source.sourceScope: User-supplied Digital Life Model100A GLB. Embedded source UID/title/CC BY-NC4 grant agree with current public artist metadata. The artist describes a generic adult female reconstructed from images and video, not a scan or a measured named individual. Actual source GLB and two1024-square embedded PNG payloads are delivered unchanged. No online archive download or source animation was acquired.
source.delivery: Original supplied GLB and embedded maps remain byte-exact. Active body palette/grain/roughness and cream baleen are disclosed separate derivatives; original eye atlas retained.193 low-profile authored barnacles attach to actual source triangles and follow their deformation. No user-photo texture projection.
source.biology: Artist generic adult female exterior compared qualitatively with NOAA gray-whale anatomy, the retained licensed whole profile photo and five private user comparisons: three live photographs and two illustrations. Not an independent taxonomic determination, specimen fit or optical calibration.
changes: Replaces the earlier generated exterior with the supplied sculpted gray-whale source, retaining original irregular skin/UV maps, eyes, dorsal knuckles, flippers, flukes, oral floor/roof and short baleen.
Existing lower anterior jaw membership is bound by actual source triangle adjacency; no new elliptical mouth, generic lip overlay, replacement baleen or source-surface cut.

Selected3.7-degree maximum small jaw aperture and minor anterior gular-floor change in a finite16-second benthic exterior study;107.5-degree right roll and -14-degree pitch are context from one northern Puget Sound study, not a fitted animal or universal strategy.

Finite12-second posterior stroke, selected distal fluke pitch and small pectoral stabilization; stopped glide and body-centred turn/side-roll studies. No source rig/clip, hydrodynamics, complete swimming or suction/filtration/swallowing simulation.

v0.6.57: replace conspicuous red-orange painted marks with selected lighter neutral adult-gray skin, preserving the artist scar pattern and adding restrained numerical grain/roughness. Separate cream baleen derivative; original source images retained in GLB.

v0.6.57:193 irregular low-profile shell approximations, with radial ridges/recessed centres, bound to actual source triangles; close inspection feature added. Not a measured infestation or complete Cryptolepas microanatomy.

v0.6.57: selected9.2-degree benthic-study jaw aperture and separate27.5-degree open-mouth anatomy study; original lower oral floor moves, upper racks and oral roof stay attached. Gape/timing unmeasured; benthic near-closed feeding and wide oral display distinguished.

viewerRig.description: Lighter neutral gray skin, attached low-profile barnacles and cream source baleen with finite source-jaw opening/closure and posterior studies. Original source surfaces/UVs retained; selected movement and skin optics uncalibrated.
viewerRig.sourceStudy: No source skeleton, morph targets or animation was supplied.

originalActive.name: original base colour and metallic-roughness on source eye material
originalActive.scope: Body/baleen source pixels preserved in GLB, replaced for active display; no original normal image.

limitations: Selected lighter adult-gray palette and193 authored attached shells are qualitative reconstructions, not an identified animal, parasite census, measured reflectance or independently validated photorealism. Source artist head/eye/blowhole proportions and natural optics remain unmeasured.

The benthic study uses a selected9.2-degree jaw aperture; a separate27.5-degree open-mouth anatomy study makes short cream baleen visible. Neither gape nor timing is measured. Near-closed benthic feeding reported in field research is distinct from a wide oral display. Full suction/tongue/hyoid/contact, sediment/prey transport, filtration, swallowing and swimming mechanics remain unfinished.

Supplied photographs are private comparison references, including duplicates, watermarked images and one labeled illustration. No supplied photo pixels are projected or redistributed. Orange cyamids occur naturally; this selected pattern removes conspicuous red-orange artist marks without asserting all gray whales lack them.
